title: Model policy deny-list is the single choke point for blocking a model across CCC and WatchTower
context: 2026-09-05: GPT-6 Astra (2.5x price) drained a weekly Codex allowance in ~30 minutes because it was the default in three places at once (the Codex CLI's own config.toml, CCC's spawn-defaults.json, and a WatchTower queue pin). WatchTower's approved-model list already excluded it, but CCC's queue editor called config.set_model directly and skipped the CLI-only check, and blank-model queues inherited CCC's default unchecked. Codex 0.153 requirements.toml has no model allow-list, so vendor-side enforcement is impossible.
decision: A machine-wide deny-list file, ~/.claude/command-center/model-policy.json ({"blocked_models": [...]}, unioned with CCC_BLOCKED_MODELS / WATCHTOWER_BLOCKED_MODELS), consulted at every spawn/resume/switch site. CCC: _model_policy_blocks wired into _model_catalog_allows_model (pickers hide), _validate_codex_model, /api/sessions/spawn for all engines, /api/queue/config (checked before any setter runs), and the codex queue-wake path. Explicit requests for a blocked model are rejected with a policy error; inherited defaults fall back to the first allowed curated model rather than failing the spawn. WatchTower reads the same file: set_model raises, model() substitutes policy_fallback_model, build_drain_command re-checks.
consequences: To use a blocked model deliberately, edit the policy file first (CCC picks it up by mtime without restart; WatchTower reads per call).
WatchTower code changes need the ai.watchtower.watcher daemon restarted; the daemon and wt CLI import the editable checkout at ~/Apps/watchtower.
Changing a queue's model via wt config retires its running worker.
Any new spawn path must go through _validate_codex_model / _model_policy_error or it silently bypasses the policy.
alternatives_rejected: Rely on Codex requirements.toml: it has no model allow-list (verified against the 0.153.4 binary).
Just change the defaults: a default is not enforcement; the next picker click or queue edit reintroduces the model.
Enforce WatchTower's hardcoded approved list at spawn time for all engines: would break kimi/other engines whose CCC defaults are not in that list; the deny-list is narrower and explicit.
Fail the spawn when an inherited default is blocked: strands queue work silently; substitution plus a ledger event keeps queues draining on an allowed model.
